new_statements.quote: Comme dans la grande majorité des langues kwa, le ton joue un rôle très important en mɔkɔle. Pour presque chaque lexème, il en existe un autre qui ne diffère que par le ton. [...] Chaque syllabe de la langue porte l’un des trois tons à niveau, soit le bas, le moyen ou le haut. [p. 262:] Sur le plan tonal, le mɔkɔle distingue trois tons simples : haut, bas et moyen. [...] Les tons peuvent se réaliser en toute position à l’exception du ton haut qui n’est pas prouvé sur les préfixes nominaux (voyelles ou nasales syllabiques).
new_statements.translation: As in the great majority of Kwa languages, tone plays a very important role in Mokole. For almost every lexeme there is another that differs only in tone. [...] Every syllable of the language bears one of the three level tones, low, mid or high. [p. 262:] Tonally, Mokole distinguishes three simple tones: high, low and mid. [...] The tones can occur in any position except that high tone is not attested on nominal prefixes (vowels or syllabic nasals).

new_statements.check: not checked by the second reader
new_statements.relation_note: A full first-hand description (20 consonants, 7 oral + 5 nasal vowels, ATR harmony, open syllables CV/V/N). Chapter 6 establishes three level lexical tones (H, M, L) by minimal pairs (afá 'penis' / afà 'arrow'; irí 'head' / iri 'song'; njò 'snake' / njo 'fear'), every syllable tone-bearing incl. syllabic nasals; tone-pattern statistics for 165 disyllabic nouns (MM 28%, MH 17%, BB 13%..) and 132 verbs; H excluded from noun-initial prefix vowels (as in all Yoruba lects, Akinkugbe 1978; H-initial CVCV nouns analysed as prefix-elided or loans); two sandhi rules only (verb L -> M before a nominal object: kpè 'call!' -> ì kpe ajá 'he called the dog'; 3sg object clitic, a copy vowel normally H, re…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Mokole is a three-level register-tone language of the Yoruba type (H, M, L on every syllable, lexically contrastive, H barred from noun prefixes, almost no tone sandhi); the description recognises no word stress or accent and does not discuss one.
new_statements.exceptions: H tone unattested on nominal prefixes (initial V- or N- of nouns); H-initial CVCV/CVV nouns treated as prefix loss or borrowings; L verb tone becomes M before a noun object; 3sg object copy-vowel H -> M after H-final verbs; long vowels analysed as two syllables, length not distinctive; interrogative final-vowel lengthening with low realisation.
new_statements.identity_note: Title, maps (ch. 3.4) and text place the language in the communes of Kandi and Malanville (Alibori), villages incl. Angaradébou, Lolo, Thui; autonym mɔkɔle, 'parler du continuum dialectal yoruba.. en discontinuité géographique avec les autres variantes' (p. 261, citing Kluge 2011: 8) = Glottolog moko1243 / ISO mkl. It is the 'mémoire de phonologie at UAC' that our bibliography wished for (item 'No specific title identified'), and the same author as A's work 0. Deposited in the UAC library repository under records 243, 4287 and 4659 (identical content).
